title: Replica placement and failure lab
description: Walk clockwise from one key and see why token positions, physical nodes, and failure domains are different counting units.

keys.label: cart:184
keys.detail: Begins beside two adjacent tokens owned by Node A.

keys.label: session:991
keys.detail: Begins beside another repeated physical owner later in the ring.

keys.label: asset:42
keys.detail: Begins in a region whose next tokens already span three nodes.

policies.label: Count token positions
policies.detail: Deliberately unsafe: adjacent virtual tokens can count the same machine twice.

policies.label: Distinct physical nodes
policies.detail: Skip virtual tokens whose physical owner is already selected.

policies.label: Spread failure domains
policies.detail: Skip repeated nodes and zones while enough independent choices exist.

incidents.label: No failure
incidents.detail: Inspect placement before injecting an outage.

incidents.label: Node A fails
incidents.detail: One physical process and all of its virtual tokens disappear.

incidents.label: Zone A fails
incidents.detail: Both Node A and Node B become unavailable together.

modelNote: The lab models placement, not quorum or consistency. A production replication strategy also owns membership convergence, repair, handoff, and topology semantics.
